newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sappi yr results postponed until next week.
newsitem.headline: Sappi yr results postponed until next week.

text.p: Pulp and paper producer Sappi Ltd said it will release its full year results on Tuesday, December 3.
The results had originally been expected this week.

JOHANNESBURG, Nov 22 (Reuter) - South African pulp and paper producer Sappi Ltd is set to produce a steep drop in year profits as it reels under the twin blows of a cyclical trough in the industry and being caught out by currency movements.
The sector, which is notoriously cyclical, has seen prices plummet to their lows in the first half of the year.

Then, as signs of a recovery started to emerge for the second half, Sappi shocked the market by issuing a profit warning saying its second half profit would be substantially lower than the first half.

The firm said forward cover on some of its export earnings taken early in the year had, because of collapsing prices and declining volumes, meant virtually all second half export sales were transacted at a much less favourable exchange rate.
"The hedging and the fact their prices have really dropped out of the bottom will both hit Sappi hard," one analyst said.

Analysts said the volatile nature of the market made profit and dividend predictions difficult. They forecast earnings per share on a range of 200 to 320 cents, against a proforma 846 cents last time.
The dividend was seen at 70 to 120 cents, against a proforma 120 last time. The comparative figures are on a proforma basis due to Sappi changing its year end date to September.
The consensus figures were for earnings of 266.6 cents a share and a dividend of 90.0 cents a share.
A spokeswoman for Sappi said the results were due early next week, but that no specific day had been decided upon.
Sappi has also suffered from problems at its Saiccor mill which has been hit by a strike and production problems.

"Saiccor is the real domestic engine and when most things have gone into the red, as they do at the bottom of the cycle, Saiccor is usually the last thing that keeps on going. But this time they had a few problems," one analyst said.
But most analysts said the last six month period should represent a low point for the group and the upturn in the cycle should start to benefit the group next year.

"If you look at the pulp and paper cycle there are some good indicators that it has turned around now and there are upticks in the prices of various products," said Mark Rule, analyst at Frankel Pollak.
